text:
Samir: Heads up — after last night's billing-db migration I'm seeing a batch of orgs with token cost = $0 or NaN on the Token Cost dashboard. Example org_id org_98765 (EU region). Totals look present but token_cost column is 0 or NaN. Screenshot: https://redwood.internal/screens/abc123

Lina: Which envs? prod only or staging too? Any common plan type for these orgs?

Samir: Prod only so far. Mostly enterprise accounts and a couple of older monthly committed plans. Happens across two dashboards (per-org tile + aggregate view).

Kevin: Looking at metering-worker logs now — seeing repeated SQL errors when joining ledger -> pricing_snapshot. Sample error from prod logs:
```
ERROR: null value in column "price_per_token" violates not-null constraint
Query: INSERT INTO computed_costs (org_id, period, token_cost) SELECT l.org_id, l.period, l.tokens * p.price_per_token FROM ledger l LEFT JOIN pricing_snapshot p ON l.plan_id = p.plan_id WHERE l.period = '2026-03-16';
```
Feels like pricing_snapshot missing rows for some legacy plan_ids after the migration.

Marta: billing-bot just posted an alert for failed pricing-sync: alert_id=A-2026-332. Could be the same issue. @billing-bot can you paste the failed partitions?

billing-bot: Failed partitions: pricing_snapshot.prod.partition_20260315 (missing plan_ids: 122, 399, 842). Retries: 3. See run: https://ci.internal/runs/77543

Lina: If pricing_snapshot is missing plan rows the join will produce NULL price_per_token which downstream code might cast to NaN when dividing. Quick triage steps:
- Reproduce by running the migrated join query for org_98765 and inspect pricing_snapshot rows for that plan_id
- Check snapshot ingestion job logs (kafka->snapshot consumer) around migration window
- If missing, backfill pricing_snapshot from pre-migration dump, then recompute computed_costs for affected periods

Samir: Repro steps I used (prod read-only):
1) SELECT count(*) FROM pricing_snapshot WHERE plan_id = 122; -- returns 0
2) Run the join SELECT l.org_id, l.tokens, p.price_per_token FROM ledger l LEFT JOIN pricing_snapshot p ON l.plan_id = p.plan_id WHERE l.org_id='org_98765' LIMIT 10; -- shows NULL price_per_token
3) Observe dashboard: /console/costs/org/98765 shows $0 and NaN rows

Kevin: I'll prepare a short backfill SQL to insert missing pricing_snapshot rows from the pre-migration export (hashed file at s3://redwood-migration/price_snapshot_pre_20260315.sql.gz). Proposed command (dry-run):
```
-- dry run
SELECT * FROM s3_import_prices('s3://redwood-migration/price_snapshot_pre_20260315.sql.gz') WHERE plan_id IN (122,399,842);
```
If good, we insert and re-run computed_costs recompute for affected orgs/periods.

Marta: Can we also add a UI fallback so that when token_cost is NULL/NaN we show "unbilled" rather than $0? Product wants to avoid misleading $0.

Lina: Yes — quick UI patch: render null as "unbilled" and add tooltip "billing data incomplete — retrying backfill". I'll open a small PR to the console to display that while we do backfill.

Samir: I started a support ticket for the customer (org_98765) explaining we have a mitigation plan (backfill + UI fallback). Ticket #SUP-1249.

Kevin: I'll run the dry-run backfill now then open a migration incident with timeline + root cause once confirmed. Will tag infra and data-eng.

Marta: Thanks — schedule for backfill + recompute in the 1hr maintenance window? We should also blacklist the recompute from triggering alerts to avoid noise.

Samir: Sounds good. Leaving notes in the incident channel after backfill. :thumbsup:
